name: workflow_interview
title: A module ask is interviewed, then drafted as "Your workflow" in the person's words

steps.say: I want help picking car wash sites to open
steps.reply: I've put that as a question card — let me know which fits (or just tell me in your own words) and I'll pick it back up from there.

steps.say: It's for me, to decide which sites to pursue and brief my investors. Sites come from brokers by email. Today I check households within 3 miles, density, drive-time population, the traffic on the road and at the main intersection, then I score fourteen things like visibility and access from 1 to 10 with a note each, and write a memo to investors. Thresholds: 45,000 households, 30,000 cars a day. Start with Austin. Go ahead and write it up.
steps.reply:
I've drafted "Your workflow" — Car wash site scorecard, Austin. It picks up where the earlier version left off: Alpha reads broker emails daily, geocodes each site, pulls households/density/drive-time population and traffic (road + intersection), checks it against your gates (45,000 households, 30,000 cars/day, and the 0.8-acre lot size from before), scores the 14 items 1–10 with notes, and drafts the investor memo — nothing gets emailed until you ask.

Four things are open on the page, each with my pick: 14 vs. 15 scorecard items (the earlier build had grown to 15), whether to keep the lot-si

steps.say: Add a minimum lot size of 0.8 acres as one of the checks.
steps.reply: Added — the 0.8-acre minimum lot size is now its own explicit gate on the page, right alongside the households (≥45,000) and traffic (≥30,000 cars/day) checks, and it's shown with its source (your own words). That also settles one of the four open questions from the last draft; three remain: 14 vs. 15 scorecard items, how listings reach Alpha (Gmail automatically vs. you pasting them in), and the drive-time window — each with my pick on the page. Let me know when you're ready to go ahead, or if there's anything else to change.

Keeps car_wash_sites, car_wash_site_scores. 3 suggestions: Reuse the Austin screener's data pipeline; Carry a status per site; Flag near-misses. Settings 6, questions 4.
